root_cause: tools/audit_shader_pipeline_inputs.py:1578 returns the base library pointer for a stage with zero constant rows. The caller then closes every handles[stage] at lines 2077/2088/2099, including that base pointer, and reuses bases[stage] in the next round. The freed AIR library is dereferenced by Library::function, producing SIGSEGV.
owner_fix: Always call bridge.tegu_air_library_specialize, including rows=[], so every returned handle is an owned clone, or track ownership and close only specialized handles. The Rust API already returns an owned clone for count=0 (regression test zero_constant_specialization_returns_an_owned_clone). Do not change the ABI.
note: Source-based caller analysis plus reproduced SIGSEGV with current bridge; no hardware/native build.
